thread:
alex: Heads-up — I’m seeing a cluster of streaming connections stuck in 'IDLE' on the dashboard. They never close and eventually count against tenant quota. Not sure if it's client-side or our proxy.

maria: I noticed a matching spike in resume attempts + duplicate session ids. Might be related to the sticky-route swap from last week's rollout. :thinking_face:

sam: Pasted a small log snippet from the proxy where we detect socket close but never garbage-collect the session: 

```
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z INFO proxy connection closed conn_id=abcd1234 session_id=sess-78
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z WARN sessions not cleaned up after close session_id=sess-78 ttl=0s
2026-03-20T14:02:40Z INFO resume token accepted session_id=sess-78 client_id=web-9
```

sam: So close happens, but then the resume path accepts a reconnection for the same session id which resurrects counters. If the connection never fully tears down we double-charge quota.

jordan: Repro steps I used locally: open ws -> force-close transport -> wait 20s -> client reconnects with same resume id -> proxy keeps old socket entry. Quick curl to repro SSE: 

```
# SSE repro (rough)
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood/test/stream?resume=sess-78" &
# then kill the pid, reconnect quickly
```

kelly: Can we add a watchdog that force-evicts idle sockets after a grace window and annotate the dashboard when we do a forced-evict? Right now the dashboard shows "active sockets" and it’s hard to tell leaked vs legitimately idle.

alex: +1. Also need a telemetry flag so we can visually separate: leaked_idle vs healthy_idle. Otherwise the quota graphs look like they're steadily rising.

maria: UX idea — add a small badge in the stream dashboard: "forced-evictions: N (last 1h)" and an explanation tooltip. Also surface the last close reason we received from the edge.

ops-bot: alert created (#streaming-watchdog-leaks) — initial threshold: 5 forced-evicts per min for any cluster. Incident playbook linked.

sam: I sketched a tiny patch to add eviction + metric: 

```
// in session_manager.go
if time.Since(s.lastSeen) > cfg.EvictionGrace {
  metrics.Inc("stream.forced_eviction")
  s.markEvicted("watchdog")
  // ensure quiesce and remove mapping
}
```

sam: Will open PR with feature flag `stream_watchdog_v1`. Suggest canary to dev cluster for 24h.

jordan: One concrete concern — forced eviction can trigger immediate resume attempts from clients and if we evict too aggressively we can create a reconnect storm. Need backoff policy baked into the eviction (tag the evicted session so resume attempts get a 'cooldown' header).

kelly: Agreed. For dashboard UX we should also add a heatmap of eviction->resume rate so SRE can tune.

alex: Also, our billing path counts a socket as billable until it's removed from the session map. If eviction removes mapping promptly we should see a drop in charge counts. Let's coordinate with billing to watch unit meter while we canary.

maria: I'll add annotations to the canary build: `watchdog.eviction=true` and link the canary in the console rollout UI with a special note: "testing eviction cooldown".

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4021 (draft). Includes metric, feature flag, and a header `X-Evicted-Reason`.

alex: Nice. Can we also add a small logline when we accept a resume for an id that was previously evicted so we can measure how often evicted sessions come back? Something like: `RESUME_AFTER_EVICT session_id=...`.

sam: yeah will add.

kelly: Ops, once PR is merged can we get a console experiment? Want a toggle so on the dashboard we can show/hide evicted counts, and a chart linking evictions -> resumed_count -> billing_delta.

ops-bot: deploy to canary cluster started. Builds: proxy@canary-evict-20260320. Estimated 20m.

maria: While canary runs, I'll attach a synthetic probe that reconnects with the old resume id after various delays to map cooldown behaviour. Will dump results to a csv and attach here.

jordan: If we see reconnect storms in probe, reduce eviction aggressiveness and increase cooldown header to clients.

alex: TL;DR action items: sam PR + feature flag, kelly dashboard badge + heatmap, maria probe + console annotation, jordan verify cooldown semantics, billing watch for meter delta.

maria: attaching initial probe output (summary): 30 forced-evicts, 7 resumes within 10s of evict, billing counter decreased by ~22 sockets after eviction cleanup. CSV in the thread (uploaded). :white_check_mark:

kelly: moving to postmortem template if this escalates. For now, canary looks promising.

alex: Thanks team. Followups tomorrow — let's avoid a global rollout until we confirm cooldown stops storming. :rocket:
